question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scope, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The internal gateway path exists, but exposing it through plugin runtime would change the public plugin contract and allow plugin code to mutate Discord bot presence through stored bot credentials.

options.title: Design gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, live Discord proof, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep message action only
options.body: Leave dynamic presence mutation on the default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this request behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a separate presence-only runtime API.

recommendation.title: Design gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, live Discord proof, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence work and can route the Discord-specific status/activity boundary with plugin-runtime reviewers.
